clue.text: Playful prank by a few

parts.note: a frolic is a merry prank or caper
some means a few, an unspecified small number

explanation.surface: Someone describes a joke pulled off by a handful of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frisky and full of fun is playful, keen on games and capers.

clue.text: Football club lost twice will go down

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the governing body of English football clubs

indicators.note: twice tells you to write the letter for lost two times over

parts.note: L is the usual abbreviation for lost in league tables

explanation.surface: A team that keeps losing is heading for relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: In football league tables L stands for lost, so 'lost twice' gives LL after FA, the Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop or descend is to go down, as prices or a team in the league can.

clue.text: The said test

definitions.meaning: spoken rather than written, as in a said agreement
a spoken examination, such as one in a language course

explanation.definitionFit: Spoken words are said rather than written, and a spoken exam is the usual short name for a viva-style test.

clue.text: Cold cabinet

parts.note: read as a chilly cupboard for keeping food, an old name for a fridge, not a hostile government

explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned refrigerator is a cupboard kept chilled with blocks of frozen water.

clue.text: A very personal form of art

definitions.text: A very personal form of art

parts.words: A very personal form of art
parts.note: personal here means literally about the person painting, an artist depicting their own face

explanation.definitionFit: An artist painting a picture of their own likeness produces the most personal kind of portrait work.

clue.text: Very little time

definitions.meaning: tiny, as an adjective pronounced my-NEWT
sixty seconds, a unit of time

explanation.definitionFit: Tiny things are extremely small, and sixty seconds make a brief unit of clock time.

clue.text: Film seen in the picture-house

indicators.note: seen in says the word can be spotted inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A movie is being watched at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand heroic movie on a large scale is called by this genre name.

clue.text: Special item

definitions.meaning: specific or out of the ordinary, as in a special case
a detail or single point, as in each item of a list

explanation.definitionFit: Something specific is special to one case, and a detail or single point is an item in a list.

clue.text: Orangeman in the Orient

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Orangeman in the Orient': the parse needs 'Orange' (definition) and 'man' (CLEMENT) as separate words, + IN + E; the held single word cannot be split.

clue.text: Do not disturb a holiday by oneself

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
alone means by oneself

explanation.surface: Someone on a solo vacation hangs out the sign asking not to be bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from bothering or interfering with someone is a common idiom for not disturbing them.

clue.text: Priceless

parts.note: read literally as costing nothing, rather than of immense value

explanation.definitionFit: Something with no price on it costs nothing, gratis.

clue.text: Vessel that should not be needed at parties?

definitions.text: Vessel that should not be needed at parties?

parts.words: Vessel that should not be needed at parties?
parts.note: a ship cutting through frozen seas, and also the game or remark that breaks awkwardness among strangers at a gathering

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that cuts through frozen seas shares its name with a party game that relaxes strangers.

clue.text: Expert in lettering working over the shop?

definitions.text: Expert in lettering working over the shop?

parts.words: Expert in lettering working over the shop?
parts.note: a craftsman who paints names on shopfronts works literally over the shop, above its door

explanation.definitionFit: A painter of fascia boards and notices is a craftsman skilled at letters.

clue.text: Favourite in advance to enter the race

indicators.note: in says the first word's synonym sits inside the second's

parts.note: to come is to advance or approach
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: The top tipped runner moves forward to join the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part in a contest or race is to vie with rivals.

clue.text: Transporter of disease?

parts.note: someone who harbours an infection and passes it on without symptoms, read as if a haulage vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A person who harbours a germ and passes it on is called by the same word as a haulage firm.

clue.text: Choose gold constituent

parts.note: to elect is to choose
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Picking a voter worth their weight in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a voter in a constituency, one who chooses the member.

clue.text: 151 at the most at the highest point

parts.note: 151 in Roman numerals is CLI
max is short for maximum, at the most

explanation.surface: A score of 151 is described as the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: The culmination or peak of a story or event is its highest point.

clue.text: Michael initially leaves Melanie perplexed for another girl

indicators.note: perplexed suggests the remaining letters are confused into a new order
leaves says a letter departs from the name Melanie
initially picks the opening letter of Michael

explanation.surface: Michael walks out on a bewildered Melanie and takes up with someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M (the first letter of Michael, said to leave by 'leaves') from MELANIE to get ELANIE, and 'perplexed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaine is a girl's name, a different one from Melanie.

clue.text: Those unable to settle could end up here

definitions.text: Those unable to settle could end up here

parts.words: Those unable to settle could end up here
parts.note: settle means pay off debts, not make a home, so this is where insolvent people go

explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent people who cannot pay what they owe are dealt with by a special tribunal.

clue.text: Breadwinner's money is deserved

definitions.meaning: income from work, as opposed to unearned income
merited, as in a well-deserved rest

explanation.definitionFit: Income from work is the worker's own, and something merited by effort is likewise won fairly.

clue.text: Be up in time for discussion

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get out of bed in time for a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read bottom to top, so the two-letter word is turned before it goes inside; 'Be up' looks like getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument with opposing sides is a structured discussion.

clue.text: Kill mother for some land

indicators.note: for here loosely tells you the mother word is set within the killing phrase

parts.note: to do in is slang for kill
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone murders their mother to get hold of an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no strong container signal: the setter leans on 'for' to show the mother goes inside the slang phrase for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory or estate is an area of land under someone's rule.

clue.text: Let Dan arrange for this treatment

indicators.note: arrange tells you to put the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let Dan book their visit to the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment of the teeth is the dentist's kind of care.

clue.text: Two priests back to back accepting one tonic

indicators.note: accepting means the pair holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest

indicators.note: back to back says the second of the pair faces the other way

parts.note: the second of the two priests, again Rev
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Two clergymen stand spine to spine while one takes a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to back' means the second clergyman faces the other way, so the pair reads as a palindrome; 'accepting' puts the numeral one in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up drink that restores one's spirits is a tonic.

clue.text: Toy bird

definitions.meaning: a plaything flown on a string in the wind
a bird of prey of the hawk family

explanation.definitionFit: A string-flown plaything and a hawk-like bird of prey share this name.

clue.text: Game of chance for a change

indicators.note: for a change suggests switching the letters of the two little words around

explanation.surface: Someone tries a gambling game just for variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling card game played against a banker.

clue.text: Yours truly on a ship eating here

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone on board a liner says where they dine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the room where sailors or soldiers take their meals.

clue.text: Salute bard ridiculously railing

indicators.note: ridiculously signals the two words are jumbled absurdly into something else

explanation.surface: Someone salutes a poet in a silly way while complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railing' looks like a verb, complaining, but is the noun: a row of posts and rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of small pillars topped by a rail forms a parapet along a stair or balcony.

clue.text: Very good but not well done

definitions.meaning: of meat, lightly cooked and still red inside

explanation.definitionFit: An exceptional thing is uncommon and fine, and lightly cooked steak is pink in the middle.

clue.text: Insubordinate insurgent left debts

parts.note: an insurgent is a rebel
IOUs are written promises to pay, debts

explanation.surface: A rebel has run off leaving behind unpaid bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Disobedient people defy authority, refusing to submit.
